clue.text: Hit and run -so negligent .

parts.note: to slap is to hit with the open hand
a dash is a short fast run

explanation.surface: A hit-and-run driver is condemned for carelessness.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapdash work is done hastily and carelessly, the way a negligent person works.

clue.text: Pop back wrapped up in dry shawl

indicators.note: the father's word is enclosed by the word for dry

parts.note: sere means dry or withered

indicators.note: back says the word for Pop is read in reverse

parts.note: pa and pop are both words for father

explanation.surface: Dad comes home bundled up in a dry wrap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop' looks like a verb but is a name for father; 'back' turns it round before it is wrapped up.
explanation.definitionFit: A serape is a brightly coloured Mexican blanket worn as a shawl.

clue.text: Island race in trouble with a conqueror

indicators.note: the race letters go into the word for trouble

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict
the TT is the motorcycle race on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: An island race runs into difficulty with an invader.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT (Tourist Trophy) is a famous motorcycle race held on the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: Attila the Hun conquered vast territories across Europe in the fifth century.

clue.text: New credit alternative for a top man

indicators.note: something new is made afresh, so the letters of credit are rearranged

parts.note: or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: A fresh line of credit offered to a senior executive.
explanation.definitionFit: A company director sits on the board, among those at the very top of the firm.

clue.text: Check some waste material

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Inspecting a portion of rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Check' looks like inspect, but it means hold back. The run is waSTE Material.
explanation.definitionFit: To stem a flow is to stop or restrain it.

clue.text: Twists the sailors on board

indicators.note: on board means aboard ship, so the sailors' word sits inside the steamship letters

parts.note: SS, steamship, stands for the ship whose board the crew is on
a ship's crew is its body of sailors

explanation.surface: A ship's crew are out of shape, twisting about on deck.
explanation.walkthrough: To be on board is to be inside the ship, so CREW goes inside SS, the abbreviation for steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: To screw something is to turn or twist it, as with a screw thread.

clue.text: Tedious job — a complaint is to be made

parts.note: a chore is a dull routine task

explanation.surface: A boring task leads to a grievance being raised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaint' means an illness here, not a grumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Chorea is a nervous disorder causing jerky movements, an ailment in the medical sense.

clue.text: About half-a dozen get notice, perhaps, and removal's arranged

indicators.note: about here means round and about, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: VI is the Roman numeral six

explanation.surface: Half a dozen tenants receive notice and their removal is organised.
explanation.definitionFit: An eviction is the legally arranged removal of tenants from their home.

clue.text: Bear with disappointing deadlock

parts.note: to stand something is to bear it
off means below par, a letdown

explanation.surface: Putting up with a frustrating impasse.
explanation.definitionFit: A standoff is a deadlock where neither side will give way.

clue.text: Some soldiers wheeled around and came back

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are a corps of the British Army
to wheel around is to turn

explanation.surface: A squad on parade wheels about and marches back.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who returned came back to where they had been.

clue.text: The stripper has to travel with the singer

parts.note: to go is to travel
a diva is a celebrated female opera singer

explanation.surface: A striptease artist tours with a vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: Lady GODIVA of legend rode naked through Coventry, so 'The stripper' is a playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Legend says Lady Godiva shed all her clothes to ride through Coventry, making her history's best-known unclothed figure.

clue.text: Infuriated by explosion of grenade

indicators.note: an explosion blows the letters of grenade apart into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is enraged by a grenade blast.
explanation.definitionFit: Angered and infuriated both mean made very cross.

clue.text: Control of river pests

parts.note: the Po is the longest river in Italy
lice are parasitic insect pests

explanation.surface: Keeping a river free of vermin.
explanation.definitionFit: To police something is to regulate or keep it under control.

clue.text: Surely conservationists should be content when it's ordered

definitions.text: Surely conservationists should be content when it's ordered

parts.words: Surely conservationists should be content when it's ordered
parts.note: to indent for goods is to place an official order for them, while the surface pictures green campaigners pleased that something is ordered

explanation.surface: Environmentalists ought to be happy when things are put in order.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition hides in 'ordered': to indent is to requisition goods, an old British commercial and military term. The rest is whimsy around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Indenting is a formal way of requisitioning supplies, so something indented has been ordered.

clue.text: Means of transport for the person unconscious of progress

definitions.meaning: a train with berths for overnight travel
one who is asleep and so unaware of what is going on

explanation.definitionFit: An overnight train with berths and a slumbering person both carry the name, one asleep while the other moves on.

clue.text: The former decay

definitions.meaning: one who forms or shapes things, as a craftsman shapes clay in a mould

explanation.definitionFit: One who moulds is a shaper or former; to rot away into dust is a separate sense of the same word.

clue.text: Idle pupil — stupid creature!

parts.note: L for learner, as on a British learner driver's plate
an oaf is a clumsy, stupid person

explanation.surface: A scolding for a lazy schoolchild.
explanation.definitionFit: To loaf is to idle about doing nothing useful.

clue.text: Having a party in the break, that's'living!

indicators.note: the party word is placed inside the word for the break

parts.note: a rent is a tear or break
a side is one party in a dispute or contest

explanation.surface: Throwing a party at half-time is the life.
explanation.definitionFit: A resident is someone living in a place, as in 'resident in London'.

clue.text: A tranquilliser, for the individual producing original work

definitions.meaning: one who composes or calms others

explanation.definitionFit: To compose is to calm as well as to create, so the one doing either shares the name.

clue.text: The landing requires illumination

definitions.meaning: coming down to settle, as a bird lights on a branch

explanation.definitionFit: To light on something is to alight or land, and the word also means the lamps that brighten a room.

clue.text: There's a famous statue to be seen in these rose-gardens

indicators.note: says the answer can be seen sitting inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A garden guide claims a celebrated sculpture stands among the roses.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'thesE ROSe'. EROS is the statue (properly of Anteros) at London's Piccadilly Circus.
explanation.definitionFit: The winged figure at Piccadilly Circus in London is popularly known by the name of the Greek love god.

clue.text: Having been ill with a seizure, get sick-pay maybe

indicators.note: ill here means badly formed, so the letters of the preceding word are rearranged

parts.note: a fit is a sudden seizure or attack

explanation.surface: After an illness and a fit, a worker claims sick-pay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having been ill' reads as an illness, but 'ill' is the anagram signal working on 'been' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Sick-pay is one example of a state or employer allowance paid out to someone in need.

clue.text: Needing a leg-up is a nuisance

indicators.note: needing help suggests the letters are in poor shape and must be put in a new order

explanation.surface: A person always needing a boost is tiresome.
explanation.definitionFit: A plague is a persistent annoyance or pest.

clue.text: End with a bit of fish and a drink

parts.note: a fin is part of a fish
ale is beer

explanation.surface: Finishing a meal with fish and beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A finale is the closing part or conclusion of a show.

clue.text: The old city is for going around another time

indicators.note: the word for 'for' surrounds the time word

parts.note: as can mean because, like for
then means at another time

explanation.surface: An ancient place may be visited again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' meaning because is a common crossword equivalence; the capital of Greece is the old city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek capital is among the oldest cities in Europe, seat of classical civilisation.

clue.text: To be engaged in land reclamation makes a badly-behaved youngster more mature

definitions.text: To be engaged in land reclamation

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
older means more grown-up

explanation.surface: Growing up turns a naughty child into someone wiser.
explanation.walkthrough: A polder is low land reclaimed from the sea, as in the Netherlands.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a polder is to wall off and drain low ground from the sea, a form of reclaiming land.

clue.text: Growth in the economy?

definitions.meaning: a plant, here the sea pink that grows on cliffs

explanation.surface: An economist asks whether the economy can grow.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea pink is a seaside plant of that name, and the word also means careful saving.

clue.text: A traveller in foreign parts must be game!

definitions.meaning: Marco ..., the Venetian who journeyed to China
a sport played on horseback with mallets

explanation.definitionFit: Marco the Venetian explorer and the horseback sport with mallets share the name.

clue.text: Standard for an American naval officer

definitions.meaning: the lowest commissioned rank in the US Navy

explanation.definitionFit: A ship's flag is one kind of standard, and the junior US Navy commissioned rank shares the name.

clue.text: Contemplate installing one in cottage being refurbished

indicators.note: the cottage letters take the numeral in, as a house installs a fitting
a refurbished building is remade, so the letters of cottage are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Thinking about putting something into a cottage under renovation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being refurbished' turns COTTAGE into COGTATE, and 'installing' places I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To cogitate is to think deeply, to ponder or contemplate.

clue.text: A revolutionary artist!

definitions.meaning: one who turns things round, such as a lathe operator
J. M. W. ..., the English landscape painter

explanation.surface: Praise for a radical painter.
explanation.definitionFit: A lathe worker shapes things by rotating them, and the great English Romantic landscape painter shares the name.

clue.text: Study progress, though not in favour of meeting.

indicators.note: says one part of the word progress is dropped and the other word takes its place

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
to con is to study or learn by heart

explanation.surface: Someone examines how things are going, without being in favour of the gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: PRO (in favour) goes out of PROGRESS and CON (study) replaces it.
explanation.definitionFit: A congress is a formal assembly or meeting of delegates.
